database._comment: No 'tables' key on purpose. base_sdk's own tables (KeyValueTable, OutboxTable, IdMappingsTable) are declared directly in the @DriftDatabase annotation in lib/src/database/app_database.dart, and the installer COPIES every table source named here into base_sdk's own package to import relatively - so listing them would compile two copies of each class. Only the migration is declared.
database._comment_migration: THE MIGRATION VERSION NUMBER IS SHARED WITH EVERY OTHER SDK IN THE APP, AND IS NOT THIS SDK'S TO COUNT ALONE. sdk_installer_base.py update_database_registration() sets the composed AppDatabase's schemaVersion to the MAXIMUM version any composed manifest declares, while each SDK writes its own `if (from < N)` guard into the one shared onUpgrade - one namespace, no allocator. Drift calls onUpgrade only when schemaVersion is GREATER than the stored user_version, so a number at or below the running maximum runs nothing at all on a device that is already there, and the column this step adds would simply never appear (productivity_sdk lost its notes table to exactly this, and this manifest's number is chosen the way that manifest's comment says to). Two further traps are specific to base: the composer SUBSTITUTES the schemaVersion getter in app_database.dart, so a base-owned number written only in Dart is erased at compose time; and max_version is only raised inside the installer's `if version and step` branch, so a version declared without a step raises nothing. Hence both, declared here. VERSIONS READ ACROSS THE FLEET BEFORE CLAIMING 19 (every manifest.json outside a .rokct/cache in every repo reachable from this workspace, read at their current main): radio_sdk 18 (agent/radio/dart), productivity_sdk 17 (productivity/productivity/dart), auth_sdk 16 (Users/auth/dart), agent_sdk 15 (agent/agent/dart), replay_sdk 15 (agent/replay/dart), subscriptions_sdk 15 (agent/subscriptions/dart), polaris_sdk 13 (corporate/polaris/dart), fav_sdk 12 (agent/fav/dart); no other manifest declares a database.migration at all - base_sdk, launch_sdk, comms_sdk and telemetry_sdk in this repo included, until now. 19 is above all of them. NOTE for whoever reads this next: radio_sdk's 17 and productivity_sdk's 17 are a LIVE COLLISION on that number (radio's own comment still records productivity at 14), which is not this PR's to fix but is the same defect all of this text is about. The step is idempotent - ensureOwnerScopeColumns() checks for the column before touching anything - and beforeOpen in app_database.dart calls it on every open as a floor, so a device that somehow skips this step still gets the column rather than throwing on its first read.

di_hooks._comment: Registers every lms profile section (student rows, partner billing/students cards, shared theme-toggle/nav-clearance) with base_sdk's ProfileSectionRegistry, plus the registry's onLogout callback - the sections base_sdk's GenericProfilePage renders on /profile and /partner-profile. Runs directly after the generated sdk-di block so GetIt already holds LmsRepository. Declared top-level, NOT in an app_type flavor block, because this SDK's Dart manifest has no flavor blocks: Supacharge is one binary serving both personas, and student-vs-partner is a runtime role - the persona split lives in the sections' visibility gates, driven by which profile route is on screen (see registerSupachargeProfileSections in the installed lms_route_pages.dart). Requires base_sdk >= 1.27.0 (the profile host with identity-header slots: the student grade badge and stat row register into the header card's badge/stats slots). Since 1.12.0 this hook also configures wallet_sdk's WalletCardSection static seam (student-persona gate + 'R' symbol) for the 'wallet.card' section wallet_sdk registers via its own di_hook - the installed lms_route_pages.dart therefore imports wallet_sdk, so compositions including lms_sdk need wallet_sdk >= 1.2.0 (the section + config seam; supacharge, this SDK's only consumer, already composes wallet_sdk).

boot_hooks._comment: Registers this SDK's bundled Afrikaans map for its manifest tr_keys into base_sdk's BundledTranslations registry at boot. Backend-served translation rows still win; the map is only the offline/unseeded fallback consulted before the humanized-key fallback. Requires a base_sdk with bundled_translations.dart.

ios.NSCalendarsUsageDescription: Your device calendar is used to sync class timetables and assignment due dates you choose to add.

boot_hooks._comment: Registers this SDK's bundled English map into base_sdk's BundledTranslations registry at boot (lms_sdk's 'af' hook is the precedent). base_sdk bundles no 'en' map because English normally survives through the humanized-key fallback, but that only holds for keys named after their copy: reset_password_text humanized to the literal "Reset password text" on every app shell's reset-password sheet, because demo builds take their served map from comms_sdk's MockSettingsRepository (a handful of rows that never carried this key). Backend-served translation rows still win; the map is only the offline/unseeded fallback consulted before the humanized-key fallback. Imports are declared explicitly (src paths, like lms_sdk) because neither symbol is exported by the auth_sdk barrel every composed main.dart already imports. Requires a base_sdk with bundled_translations.dart (the bundled-af wave).

di_hooks._comment: Registers the 'wallet.card' profile section (base_sdk's BaseWalletCard composed with this SDK's history/top-up routes and Send sheet) with base_sdk's ProfileSectionRegistry - the wallet card base_sdk's GenericProfilePage renders on any composed profile route. Declared top-level, NOT in an app_type flavor block, mirroring marketplace_sdk's marketplace-profile-sections hook. Configuration rides WalletCardSection's static seam (visible / symbol / extraActions / showActions), set by a home SDK's own di_hook. Order 20 leaves room for a lower-order home-SDK hook to configure the seam before registration - though the builder and gate also re-read the seam on every page mount, so a later hook still takes effect. Requires base_sdk >= 1.23.0 (the profile host) and >= 1.33.0 (BaseWalletCard `wallet` param).

migration.step: if (from < 15) { await m.createTable(lessonProgressTable); await m.createTable(downloadedAssetsTable); } if (from < 23) { await ensureReplayOwnerScopeColumns(this); }

database._comment: 23 is replay_sdk's owner-scoping version in the shared fleetwide namespace. lesson_progress_table gains an `owner` column inside its primary key so two accounts on one device do not resume each other's lessons; the step rebuilds the table (rename aside, recreate, copy the shared columns, drop) because SQLite cannot alter a primary key in place, and carried rows take the '' default, which stays visible to everyone. downloaded_assets_table indexes files on the device's own disk, not a user's data, and is left unscoped.

migration.step: if (from < 15) { await m.createTable(assistantCacheTable); await m.createTable(assistantHistoryTable); } if (from < 21) { await ensureAgentOwnerScopeColumns(this); }

database._comment: 21 is agent_sdk's owner-scoping version in the shared fleetwide namespace. assistant_history_table gains an `owner` column inside its primary key so two accounts on one device cannot read each other's transcripts; the step rebuilds the table (rename aside, recreate, copy the shared columns, drop) because SQLite cannot alter a primary key in place, and carried rows take the '' default, which stays visible to everyone. assistant_cache_table is content, not user data, and is left unscoped.

boot_hooks._comment: Windows notification delivery, POS parity (1.6.0): firebase_messaging has no Windows implementation, so the FCM hook above deliberately excludes Windows and composed Windows exes shipped with NO notification path at all. This hook starts comms' DesktopNotificationPoller (10s REST count polling + looping POS notification.wav + ValueNotifier badge feed - see the service's doc comment) on Windows only. The start is deferred to addPostFrameCallback because boot-hook bodies run BEFORE LocalStorage.init() and the sdk-di block in the generated main.dart: by first frame both are done, and runApp is never delayed by a poll. Fail-open try/catch like the FCM hook - a boot failure debugPrints instead of blanking the app. WidgetsBinding resolves via main.dart's static material import; foundation dedupes with the FCM hook's wiring import. Toast layer (still 1.6.0, same unmerged PR): poller.start() also initializes LocalNotifications fail-open (flutter_local_notifications 19.x WindowsInitializationSettings - stable hardcoded GUID, APP_NAME/WINDOWS_AUMID dart-defines for branding, works unpackaged; MSIX identity optional host-side) and each count increase raises a native toast via LocalNotifications.show() alongside the sound - no hook body change needed, the toast path lives entirely inside the service.

database._comment_migration:
THE MIGRATION VERSION NUMBER IS SHARED WITH EVERY OTHER SDK IN THE APP, AND IS NOT THIS SDK'S TO COUNT ALONE. The composer sets the composed AppDatabase's schemaVersion to the MAXIMUM version any composed manifest declares (sdk_installer_base.py update_database_registration) while each SDK writes its own `if (from < N)` guards, so the numbers live in one namespace with no allocator. auth_sdk (Users/auth/dart/manifest.json) already declares 16 for offlineUsersTable, so the composed launcher was ALREADY at schemaVersion 16 while this manifest still said 15 - and the 1.6.0 bump 15 -> 16 therefore raised nothing. Drift only calls onUpgrade when schemaVersion is greater than the stored user_version, so on any device that had the previous launcher installed no upgrade ran at all, notes_table was never created, and every note insert failed on `no such table`. Notes are created at 17 for that reason. When adding a table here, claim a version HIGHER than any other composed manifest's - never merely one above this SDK's own last number.

OWNER SCOPING, VERSION 20 (2026-09-20). Every table this manifest registers gained an `owner` column IN ITS PRIMARY KEY, so two accounts on one device cannot see each other's rows - the follow-up to core PR #254, which did the same for base_sdk's KeyValueTable and OutboxTable at version 19. 20 was reserved for this change fleetwide and is above every number in the field (base_sdk 19, radio_sdk 18, this SDK's own previous 17, auth_sdk 16). VISIBILITY SCOPING, NEVER DELETION: the step destroys nothing and guesses no owner - carried-over rows take the '' default and come out UNOWNED, which the visibility rule `owner = '' OR owner = <me>` treats as the current account's, so every row already on a device stays exactly as visible as it is today. The step rebuilds each table the long way round (rename aside, create from the current Dart definition, copy the shared columns, drop) because SQLite cannot alter a primary key in place; ensureProductivityOwnerColumns() lives in tasks_table.dart because the composer copies only the files named under `tables` into base_sdk's package, and it is idempotent, so running it here, in this SDK's own floor (ProductivityOwnerScope.ready, awaited by every read and write) or in both comes to the same thing. notes_table's create moved from `from < 17` to this step for the rule the test below pins: the newest work is done at the top version, so no device sits between the two numbers and misses it. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING COLLISION, not fixed here: radio_sdk (RokctAI/agent radio/dart) also declares 17, the number this manifest used to hold.

migration.step: if (from < 13) { await m.createTable(tasksTable); } if (from < 14) { await m.createTable(recoveryProfilesTable); await m.createTable(avoidedHabitsTable); await m.createTable(urgeLogsTable); await m.createTable(dailyRitualsTable); await m.createTable(ritualLogsTable); await m.createTable(procrastinationLogsTable); } if (from < 15) { await m.addColumn(tasksTable, tasksTable.clientId); await m.addColumn(tasksTable, tasksTable.remoteId); } if (from < 20) { await m.createTable(notesTable); await ensureProductivityOwnerColumns(this, <TableInfo<Table, dynamic>>[tasksTable, notesTable, recoveryProfilesTable, avoidedHabitsTable, urgeLogsTable, dailyRitualsTable, ritualLogsTable, procrastinationLogsTable]); }

boot_hooks._comment: Order 30: after comms' Firebase/FCM boot (10) and its desktop notification poller (20) - order 20 is already taken and duplicate orders draw a composer warning. Android-only and fail-open like comms' hooks. The initialize() call itself is a strict no-op unless DeviceServices proves the device GMS-free AND HMS-capable, so GMS devices and detection errors keep comms_sdk's FCM path as the sole push owner. The await is cheap: initialize() only awaits the availability probe and turnOnPush - the push token arrives asynchronously on Push Kit's token stream, so runApp is never delayed by a token round-trip.
